serre_hilbert_required_place_rule.input: one fixed finite family of rational squareclasses alpha_i and one fixed finite family beta_j that are actually paired by local Hilbert symbols
serre_hilbert_required_place_rule.normalization: choose squarefree rational representatives; only valuation parity and real sign matter
serre_hilbert_required_place_rule.finite_places: 2 together with every odd prime q for which some alpha_i or beta_j has odd q-adic valuation
serre_hilbert_required_place_rule.required_place_set: S_Hilb={infinity,2} union {odd q : some v_q(alpha_i) or v_q(beta_j) is odd}
serre_hilbert_required_place_rule.outside_set_reason: for odd q outside S_Hilb every alpha_i and beta_j is a q-adic unit; the odd-prime Hilbert-symbol formula gives (alpha_i,beta_j)_q=+1 for every pair

stage36_instantiation_check.why_Xi_support_alone_is_insufficient: the relevant Serre place set depends on both entries of the fixed Hilbert pairing; Xi_BT alone does not determine primes introduced by the second entry
stage36_instantiation_check.why_receiver_bad_places_are_insufficient: receiver bad places classify local geometry of the BT cover, not the theorem-specific support of a fixed Hilbert pairing or Poitou-Tate local-condition system
stage36_instantiation_check.why_CK_good_prime_family_does_not_force_: once a fixed pairing system is supplied, odd primes outside the finite valuation-parity support have automatically trivial Hilbert symbols; this finite-support reduction is conditional on the missing second-side pairing data
